questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Matrix
questions.problem: Find $B=\overset{―}{A}$, where $A=[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} & 6+4\text{i} \\ 7-4\text{i} & 4+9\text{i}\end{aligned}].$ What is the value of ${b}_{12}-{b}_{21}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} & 6+4\text{i} \\ 7-4\text{i} & 4+9\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{7-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{6+4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{7-4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4+9\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7+\text{i} & 6-4\text{i} \\ 7+4\text{i} & 4-9\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{12}-{b}_{21}=(6-4\text{i})-(7+4\text{i})=-1-8\text{i}.$

questions.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}3\text{i} & -2+2\text{i} & 5-5\text{i} \\ \text{i} & -1+5\text{i} & -3+4\text{i} \\ -5-3\text{i} & 4-4\text{i} & 4\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-2+2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{5-5\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-1+5\text{i}} & \overset{―}{-3+4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-5-3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4-4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{4\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3\text{i} & -2-2\text{i} & 5+5\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & -1-5\text{i} & -3-4\text{i} \\ -5+3\text{i} & 4+4\text{i} & -4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${b}_{12}+{b}_{23}=(-2-2\text{i})+(-3-4\text{i})=-5-6\text{i}.$

questions.problem: If $\,\text{Re}(x)=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,\text{Im}(x)=[\begin{aligned}e & f \\ g & h\end{aligned}]\,$ are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3-9\text{i} & -7+\text{i} \\ -5-2\text{i} & -4\text{i}\end{aligned}]\,$ then what is the value of $bc-ef?$
questions.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-3-9\text{i} & -7+\text{i} \\ -5-2\text{i} & -4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\ A & =[\begin{aligned}-3-9\text{i} & -7+\text{i} \\ -5-2\text{i} & 0-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ -5 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-9 & 1 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $b=-7,c=-5,e=-9$ and $f=1.$ Therefore,

$$
bc-ef=(-7)\cdot (-5)-(-9)\cdot 1=44.
$$

$$

questions.problem:
Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3 & \text{i}\end{aligned}]$, find the result of applying to $A$ the following elementary row operations: 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's apply the row operations to $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3 & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ -3+\frac{3}{1+\text{i}}\cdot (1+\text{i}) & \text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & \text{i}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & \text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i} & \text{i}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{2-\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ -2+\text{i}+\frac{(2-\text{i})(1+2\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}} & \text{i}+\frac{(2-\text{i})(1+\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & \frac{(\text{i}-2)+(3+\text{i})}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the result  is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Matrix
canonical_examples.problem: Find $B=\overline{A},$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/25ce0cd375da320d1615cf49f659ec33e4646cf6bc66455198bec5fd591b3dd3.png) What is the value of $b_{11} + b_{23}?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Taking the complex conjugate of each entry, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{A} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} & 3-\text{i} & 1+\text{i} \\ 2-2\text{i} & 2-\text{i} & 1+2\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 3\text{i} & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{4\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1+\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{2-2\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2-\text{i}} & \overset{―}{1+2\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{\text{i}} & \overset{―}{3\text{i}} & \overset{―}{2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} & 3+\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ 2+2\text{i} & 2+\text{i} & 1-2\text{i} \\ -\text{i} & -3\text{i} & -2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $b_{11} + b_{23} = (-4\textrm{i}) + (1-2\textrm{i}) = 1-6\textrm{i}.$

canonical_examples.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/3e677aa7f2db1cc637e0566a60813ebae1e2bccf80325106317c1d2b7717c2a5.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/67a421166c674275ae14da43962c8e5c8ea37b6a9c8a0548d5b09428b703d831.png) are the real and imaginary parts of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14045065/assets/fde83769f627e95f5dfe3285bf275ebfe1678710a36c264b6662248063470bb0.png) then what is the value of $ad+eh?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For the given matrix $A,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2-3\text{i} & -5-7\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} & 5-9\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(A)}+\text{i}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ -6 & -9\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(A)}.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $a=2,d=5,e=-3$ and $h=-9.$ Therefore,

$$
ad+eh=2 \cdot 5 + (-3) \cdot (-9) = 37.
$$

Multiplying the matrices using the usual method, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & \text{i} \\ 1 & 2\text{i}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} & 1-\text{i} \\ \text{i} & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-\text{i})\cdot (1+2\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & (-\text{i})\cdot (1-\text{i})+\text{i}\cdot 2 \\ 1\cdot (1+2\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot \text{i} & 1\cdot (1-\text{i})+2\text{i}\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(2-\text{i})+(-1) & (-1-\text{i})+2\text{i} \\ (1+2\text{i})+(-2) & (1-\text{i})+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} & -1+\text{i} \\ -1+2\text{i} & 1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
